text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT INC-20260315-01 — Elevated p95 token latency on /v1/generate (hosted). Trigger: p95 token latency > 1200ms over 5m. Affected region: us-west-2. Initial symptom: sustained queue depth on runtime workers. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/runtime-batching. Paging eng-oncall.
Alex: ack, I'm looking. pulling recent runtime traces and sproc logs.
Sam: seeing continuous-batching queue spikes on infer-rt-*. gpu_util 94%, p95 token latency 1.3s, 5xx up from 0.3% to 1.6%. logs snippet: ```[2026-03-15T09:12:10Z] queue_len=124 batch_sz_avg=22 gpu_util=94% latency_p95=1320ms```
Priya: quick triage — looks like worker-side batching is building because producers are bursty and autoscaler hasn't added nodes fast enough. Two live mitigations we can try: 1) traffic shaping/rate-limit non-critical tenants to take immediate pressure off; 2) change continuous batching params to favor throughput (bigger batches) which reduces compute overhead but will increase tail latency. Given overall 5xx increase, I'd prefer to prioritize throughput so we avoid dropped requests.
Maria: FYI we have 3 paying tenants in the affected region flagged as "interactive". Support already alerted customers. If we increase batch timeouts they may notice higher latency but fewer failures.
Alex: what's the exact config change? small patch we can roll out to canary pool first?
Priya: propose apply to canary (10% traffic) first: 
```yaml
continuous_batching:
  max_batch_size: 64
  batch_timeout_ms: 150
  max_queued_requests: 1000
  enable_prefill: true
```
This trades latency -> throughput (p95 expected to move up, but p99 shouldn't spike too much), throughput should increase and 5xx should drop. Also apply per-tenant dynamic rate limit for free tier: 5rps.
Sam: will add rate-limit rule to routing policy: `PUT /admin/route/rate-limits` with payload to set free tier to 5rps. I'll push that first — lower risk and immediate effect.
Sam: command I'm running now: ```curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/api/v1/route/rate-limits" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"scope":"free-tier","requests_per_second":5}'```
Sam: applied rate-limit, starting to see queue drop within 30s. queue_len now 48.
Alex: applying batching config to canary group (canary id: canary-rt-02). running rollout: ```POST /admin/runtime/configs/continuous-batching/apply?group=canary-rt-02``` payload above.
Alex: applied to canary. prewarm and observing metrics.
incident-bot: SYSTEM: config-rollout started for canary-rt-02 by Alex (rollout id ROLL-987).
Sam: canary metrics after 90s: throughput +2.1x, 5xx -> 0.4% (good), p95 increased to ~1600ms for canary. overall queue depth in canary workers down 60%.
Maria: customer impact note: support pipeline — notifying interactive tenant owners: "We applied temporary mitigations to reduce errors which may increase latency up to ~300ms for interactive workloads. Monitoring ongoing."
Priya: plan: if canary looks stable for 5m, we roll to 50% then 100% with a 10m wait and watch. if errors drop but p95 is unacceptable for top-tier customers, we will carve out them from the throughput-optimized policy (pin them to smaller batch config).
Alex: promoting to 50% now.
incident-bot: SYSTEM: Rollout to 50% complete.
Sam: after 5m at 50%: global 5xx back to baseline 0.25%, throughput improved cluster-wide, GPU util down to 78% average, overall request latency p95 median moved from 1300ms->1450ms.
Priya: Good — reduced errors. Next step: create exception for top-tier interactive customers. Sam, can you add an override routing rule to send their traffic to lite-batching config?
Sam: adding override for tenants: T-42, T-314. payload: `{ "tenant_id": ["T-42","T-314"], "batching_profile": "low-latency" }` applied.
Maria: Support will update those tenants. Also starting an incident bridge for postmortem.
Alex: handing off active pager to Priya for next 45m. I'm out for a short break but monitoring alerts.
Priya: taking ownership. I'll keep watch and coordinate follow-ups. quick note for the postmortem: collect sampling from pre and post rollout, including per-tenant p95/p99 and 5xx. Also check autoscaler logs to see why nodes didn't scale earlier.
Support Bot: Noted — customer messages queued for T-42 and T-314. Support escalation created SEV-1587.
Priya: we should also add an automated playbook entry: when queue_len > 100 for 3m, auto-apply rate-limit to non-paid tiers and trigger a canary batching config change. I'll create a ticket.
Alex: lgtm. one more thing — schedule a follow-up in 2 hours to confirm rollback/keep policy.
Maria: adding calendar invite. closing thread updates here when done. :white_check_mark:
